hot.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
hot.summary: Priming Models train a one-step image generator by first reconstructing clean images from corrupted inputs, then matching generated and real examples in frozen feature space. On ImageNet, Priming-L reaches FID 1.19 in one network pass using 238.95 EFLOPs, versus Drifting-L’s FID 1.61 using 1,476.39 EFLOPs. This is about 6.2 times less reported training compute for this comparison only.

hot.title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
hot.summary: Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks is examined through neuron- and circuit-level studies of image models and language models, including experiments that track neurons during training and test explanations through activation examples, interventions, and attribution graphs. hot.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
hot.summary: The authors survey agentic robots as systems that use goals, observations, capabilities, and execution feedback to choose actions, gather information, revise plans, or recover. They organize prior work into four domains and seventeen overlapping categories. An external RoboDojo evaluation reports 22.48% average success across 42 simulation tasks, versus 19.34% for trained DM0.5; this comparison does not isolate feedback’s effect.

hot.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
hot.summary: RePR trains image representations to capture how context improves a generative predictor’s predictions of image patches. It uses this signal to guide a tokenizer, then generates pixels from that representation. On ImageNet, 50,000 generations yield FID 2.18 for RePR-78M plus JiT-L versus 2.36 for pixel JiT-L at nearly matched training compute. This compares training FLOPs, not inference cost.

hot.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
hot.summary: HybridAgent lets a tool-using language-model agent reason in continuous hidden states and use text for tool calls and answers. HybridLink aligns hidden states with the model’s input-embedding space, while retained attention-cache entries carry context across turns. At 14B parameters, it scores 49.5 average on WebWalker versus ARPO’s 40.5, within evaluations of Qwen3-Base models on 11 benchmarks.

hot.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
hot.summary: AutoSFT helps an agent improve supervised fine-tuning by changing training data through a structured research loop. A meta-agent selects recipes, while separate execution and analysis agents handle training and propose data changes; synthesis adds verified examples. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, analysis reaches 67.10 on IFEval versus 60.60 within 30 rounds, in single searches per configuration.

hot.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
hot.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents through alternating cycles of verified self-rewriting and policy refinement. It preserves successful demonstrations to update the actor, then uses execution feedback to refine the policy while carrying a learned value critic across phases. Across four Terminal-Bench suites, the equal-weight Mean@3 rises from 20.68% to 50.58%; on LHTB, strict completions rise from 0/46 to 5/46.

hot.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
hot.summary: ATAS addresses screenplay-to-video continuity by storing static scene geometry and time-indexed event evidence for later shots. Validation separates film inclusion from memory updates. ATAS reports 15.968 PSNR_C on spatial revisit, versus ViewCrafter’s 15.255, and leads three event-recapture axes but trails ReCA on action-and-state preservation; event tests use no synchronized target video.

hot.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
hot.summary: VideoJev scores candidate time intervals to locate events and candidate answers for video questions, reusing one video prefix across queries through cached or joint inference. It reports 65.3 mean temporal intersection-over-union, versus 58.6 for its 4B backbone, and a four-benchmark QA mean of 74.3, near 74.9 for Qwen3.5-4B Thinking; evaluations cover grounding and multiple-choice QA, not agent workflows.

hot.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
hot.summary: The authors test whether resetting search history helps agents improve stalled optimization tasks. They periodically clear agent sessions and candidate-history state while retaining the best candidate, allowing four-agent teams to restart exploration. On AHC014, forgetting gains 9.2% on average over 30 more proposals per agent, versus 1.4% for continuing; experiments do not isolate which cleared state drives the gain.

hot.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
hot.summary: T2-Z adapts an action-conditioned world model to hidden environmental variation by optimizing a compact latent from observed interaction trajectories, without labels for hidden factors. The trained model stays frozen during test-time adaptation. Across four real-world tasks, average tracked-state prediction error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels and action success rose from 26.47% to 70.80%; these are task averages, not guarantees.

hot.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: The authors benchmark ten self-distillation methods against GRPO across four tasks and Qwen3.5 models at 2B, 4B, and 9B, using a shared evaluation protocol. Across twelve task-model settings, PCSD has the highest equal-weight mean, 54.26 versus GRPO’s 49.68, but leads no individual setting, winning six, trailing five, and tying one; results are limited to this benchmark.

hot.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
hot.summary: Player-1 trains a computer-use model for game control by extending screenshot-based inputs with view turning, sustained, and concurrent actions, then using verifiable rewards in 16 synthetic environments to refine a demonstration-trained policy. On MineDojo-300, Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% task success after reinforcement learning, versus 10.54% after supervised fine-tuning; these benchmark results do not establish universal game competence.

hot.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
hot.summary: Intern-Decision scores multiple typed choices in one multimodal model pass, returning structured labels and probabilities. It places decision placeholders in a JSON schema and reads legal-option scores from logits before each placeholder, avoiding answer-by-answer decoding. Across seven benchmark suites, Intern-Decision-4B averages 90.02%, versus Jev’s 88.74%; this is an evaluated-systems comparison, not evidence that joint scoring caused the gain.

hot.title: CyberArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat
hot.summary: CyberArena evaluates cybersecurity agents in reciprocal contests: two agents attack and patch identical vulnerable services over three rounds, and defensive changes persist. A latent-ability model adjusts scores for opponents and challenges. On 30 challenges all three comparison models solved solo, round-three capture rates were 52%, 37%, and 35%; these rates do not establish patching as the sole cause.

hot.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
hot.summary: The method lets one pretrained encoder serve different compute budgets by ranking its MLP neurons and attention heads, then removing lower-ranked units without retraining or updating model weights. At 50% FLOP sparsity, DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 retains 84.4% ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy, down 0.8 percentage points, while removing 427 million parameters. Deep pruning remains difficult for evaluated decoder-based text embedders.

hot.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
hot.summary: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed-forward novel-view rendering by keeping geometry-derived Gaussian centers fixed while learning opacity, shape, and color. Its training aligns cameras and emphasizes larger-angle target views, allowing attributes to improve renderings without moving points. Across six datasets, pose-conditioned mean LPIPS is 0.2472 and DISTS is 0.1163; severe errors in predicted geometry remain uncorrected.

hot.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: Spark-0 uses tactile demonstrations to train visual features to represent contact and conditions its action generator on touch when sensors are available. In a pretraining comparison, Ego Humanoid success without touch at deployment rises from 52.45% to 71.72% with 1,000 hours of tactile data. This supports retaining touch during pretraining, but does not isolate which route causes the gain.

hot.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
hot.summary: LatentLoop reallocates computation in looped MoE models by compressing the sequence for the first visit, writing its update back to full resolution, and processing the full sequence on the second visit. Across 15 matched configurations, it has lower validation negative log-likelihood than baselines. Fitted curves predict 19.0% and 7.9% less training computation at equal loss, within the observed allocation range.

hot.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
hot.summary: Speculative Forcing reduces denoising work for video and interactive world generation by predicting when latent video tokens are ready to stop, while continuing to refine others. In 5-second LongLive generation, it averages 1.68 evaluations per token versus 4.00 and measures 41.74 versus 26.40 frames per second, with VBench Total scores of 83.21 versus 83.08. These measurements are specific to this evaluation.

likes.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce a corrector for diffusion image generation that refines the denoiser’s clean-image prediction before each sampling update. Trained on the denoiser’s own predictions, the corrector can be applied repeatedly. On class-conditional ImageNet-256 with DiT-XL/2 at 250 network evaluations, it lowers FID-50K from 9.58 unguided to 2.07, versus 2.51 for CFG, with lower precision but higher recall than CFG.

likes.title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
likes.summary: NCM generates text by encoding it into hierarchical discrete representations and predicting them coarse to fine, with codes at each level generated in parallel. It reports LM1B generative perplexity of 93.05 at 12 function evaluations, compared with DUO’s 97.30 at 128, alongside similar measured diversity and a reported 21× wall-clock speedup. These results are benchmark-specific, and larger-scale behavior remains open.

likes.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
likes.summary: RSI-Anything uses predicted outcomes to select actions for testing, then pairs predictions with observed results to guide policy updates and conditional world-model adaptation. With the coder fixed on CodeContests, hidden-test all-pass success rose from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% with fixed-model selection and 31.2% with adaptation, at similar online test usage. This does not establish sustained joint improvement.

likes.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
likes.summary: Vela turns users’ timestamped behavior histories into supervision for predicting future actions and answering rubric-scored questions grounded in past evidence. It separates visible history from future outcomes to avoid leaking prediction targets. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Vela-Instruct raises VelaBench from 51.5 to 63.0, but this shows gains after training on behavior-derived data, not that behavior supervision alone caused them.

likes.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
likes.summary: ReplaySSM reduces recurrent-state writes during state-space model decoding by keeping a checkpoint and buffering recent inputs, then periodically folding them into the checkpoint. It also supports pointer-based speculative rollback and separate low- and high-precision checkpoints. At batch size 256, whole-model decode latency improved 1.20–1.47× across four hybrid models; gains depend on setup and batch size, and checkpoint reads remain.

likes.title: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents
likes.summary: AutoEnvScaling makes terminal-environment design part of reinforcement learning: a proposer inspects solver failures, builds and tests tasks in a sandbox, then refreshes the training pool using solver feedback. Admission checks filter tasks but do not guarantee correct tests. On held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B reaches avg@5 38.9 versus 34.6 with a matched static pool; finite-run results do not establish indefinite improvement.

likes.title: AlphaNIST: Emergent Assembly Skills from Binary Task Rewards
likes.summary: AlphaNIST tests whether one shared policy can learn varied assembly tasks without prescribed strategies. It trains across parts and starts using a binary completion reward alongside a control cost. At 64K environments and 25K iterations, shared sparse-reward training reaches 98.2% success, versus 81.4% for separate policies. These are training results; hardware transfer and assembling all 20 pairs in one episode remain untested.

likes.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
likes.summary: Prompteina lets designers specify global and residue-level protein goals in natural language, then generates structure and sequence together. Its text pathways combine shared context with residue-level control. In a GM2A campaign, 9 of 89 tested designs were classified as binders; the strongest had an apparent dissociation constant of 107 nM across three replicates, validating binding for selected designs against one target.

likes.title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
likes.summary: LFD adapts a flow generator to natural-language scientific goals by having a frozen LLM propose attainable sub-goals and judge sampled candidates, then training on positive-versus-negative preferences. It repeats this process as the generator changes. In GSK3β ATP-pocket design, LFD reached a mean GNINA CNNaffinity of 6.77 ± 0.11 pK, above reward-guided baselines; this is computational docking evidence, not experimental validation.

likes.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
likes.summary: The authors introduce an executable-verifier hardening method combining an isolated sandbox with an online hacker–fixer loop. The hacker searches with verifier-source access; the fixer repairs checks, then tests legitimate solutions. On 102 selected Terminal Bench tasks, Opus 5’s unhinted per-trial attack success rate fell from 69.9% to 12.1%, while benign solve rate changed from 93.1% to 91.2%; this does not establish that all vulnerabilities are closed.

likes.title: Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
likes.summary: Artisan generates articulated 3D assets by assigning planning, construction, and review to separate agents, then using simulator checks to guide repairs. In a GPT-5.6-Sol ablation, removing physical validation raised sampled single-joint collision rates from 1.9% to 35.7% and multi-joint rates from 16.4% to 73.2%. These tests cover sampled configurations, not every possible pose.

likes.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge
likes.summary: The authors introduce interaction-based evaluation: a computer-use agent operates an app, and a judge assesses the resulting trace. Gemini 3 Flash reaches 69.1% accuracy on pairwise preferences, versus 65.6% with code alone. GPT 5.6 Sol reaches 81.6% on requirement verification, versus 77.0%. Interaction feedback also repairs more initially broken requirements within five iterations, while requirement discovery remains difficult.

likes.title: ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents
likes.summary: The authors present ProgramGym, which builds behavior-checked training environments for source-free program reproduction and pairs them with a staged agent workflow. The workflow separates exploration, implementation, and review, while persistent records carry evidence between stages. On ProgramBench, Qwen3.8-27B with Program-Agent scores 55.71% Tests Passed versus 34.87% with Claude Code, but resolves only 0.50% of tasks.

likes.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
likes.summary: Cowork-Gym generates environments for agents working with people through shared files and tools. It builds tasks, workspaces, user policies, and hybrid checks, then runs and revises environments; simulated users respond to progress and can change inputs. Qwen models improve in most comparisons; Ours-27B scores 0.8400 on PawBench under OpenClaw, but WildClawBench is a weakness and the pool is not representative.

likes.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs
likes.summary: CaRe addresses audio-visual errors where a correct modality-specific answer is lost in the joint prediction. A text-only probe nominates audio or video; if the unimodal and joint answers disagree, CaRe steers the joint representation toward the unimodal reference while retaining both modalities. On CMM, MiniCPM-o-2.6 reaches 86.9% accuracy versus MAD’s 77.3%; evidence is limited to discrete-answer cross-modal hallucination benchmarks.

likes.title: World Modeling through Spectral Alignment
likes.summary: SpecWM trains visual world models by making pairwise observation similarities an explicit target for latent representations, including a temporal target based only on distance between observations in a trajectory. Its action-conditioned predictor supports goal-image planning with CEM. On OGBench Scene, temporal SpecWM achieves 77% success versus 49% for LeWorldModel; gains are benchmark-specific, not evidence of faster or cheaper planning.

likes.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals
likes.summary: MSAR lets Transformer layers retrieve earlier representations through multiple contextual views. It applies causal convolutions to single-stream sources, performs separate depth retrieval for each view, then fuses the results into one layer input. In the authors’ DeepSeekMoE-style experiments, it leads tested baselines on all 12 benchmarks at 18B and 28B; results are limited to these evaluated models and setup.
